chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who purchased a ram and it perished from him. He said: “He should purchase another in its place.”

I said: “What if he purchases another in its place, then finds the first one?” He said: “If both are still standing alive, then let him slaughter the first and sell the other; and if he wishes, he may slaughter it as well. And if he has already slaughtered the other, then let him slaughter the first along with it.”

key_terms.فَلْيَذْبَحِ: then he should slaughter, indicating the legal instruction
key_terms.فَهَلَكَ: it perished or was lost in a way that prevented its use
key_terms.كَبْشًا: a ram intended here as a sacrificial animal
key_terms.مَكَانَهُ: in its place, as a replacement
key_terms.وَ لْيَبِعِ: and he should sell, referring to the disposal of the extra animal
key_terms.ٱلْآخَرَ: the other, meaning the replacement animal
key_terms.ٱلْأَوَّلَ: the first, meaning the original animal purchased

ai.seo_question: What should be done if a sacrificial ram is replaced and then the original animal is found?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a sacrificial ram that is thought to have perished, leading its owner to buy a replacement. If the original is later found, the Imam عليه السلام explains which animal fulfills the obligation and what may be done with the other, clarifying the practical rulings of sacrificial replacement.
